ownedMethodContentMember.name: Review project structure and generated templates
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Review project structure and generated templates

step.sectionDescription: Inspect template, source, configuration, documentation, and pipeline files in the artifact explorer.
Identify entry points, Lambda handlers, infrastructure resources, parameters, outputs, and generated deployment instructions.
Compare the generated structure with the PSM deployable slice and record missing or unexpected components.
Create a dedicated branch or repository according to team policy.
Commit the unmodified generated baseline with generator, PSM revision, and generation timestamp recorded.
Tag or otherwise identify the baseline so later refinements are reviewable.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: Route structural gaps back to the PSM
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Route structural gaps back to the PSM

step.sectionDescription: Classify each gap as a PSM modeling defect, generator limitation, or legitimate implementation refinement.
For missing resources, permissions, integrations, or policies, update and validate the PSM before regenerating artifacts.
Record the reason for any approved hand-maintained template extension.
Add repository documentation, ownership, license, ignore rules, and contribution instructions required by the organization.
Confirm generated documentation names the service, supported environments, and deployment prerequisites.
Ensure build outputs and local credentials are excluded from source control.
List required parameters, outputs, domains, regions, account IDs, tags, feature flags, and external endpoints.
Provide validated values or references for development, test, staging, and production.
Document defaults, allowed ranges, and the owner for every environment-specific value.
Replace inline credentials, tokens, and sensitive defaults with approved secret-manager or parameter-store references.
Verify encryption keys, rotation expectations, and access paths for each secret or protected data store.
Document bootstrap steps that create secrets before deployment.
Review execution roles, resource policies, and CI/CD identities against least-privilege requirements.
Separate deployment permissions from application runtime permissions.
Record exceptions, approval owners, and expiration dates for elevated access.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: Implement repeatable build and deployment pipeline
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Implement repeatable build and deployment pipeline

step.sectionDescription: Configure the approved CI/CD workflow to restore dependencies, build, package, validate, and deploy the artifact.
Pin or record runtime, build-image, and dependency-resolution versions.
Require review and controlled promotion between environments.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: Run reproducible build and infrastructure validation
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Run reproducible build and infrastructure validation

step.sectionDescription: Build and package the project using the delivery pipeline.
Run the project's infrastructure/template validation and capture the results.
Verify generated deployment artifacts match the tagged source revision.
Run approved dependency, secret, and infrastructure security scans.
Triage findings by severity and exploitability; fix blockers or obtain time-bound risk acceptance.
Verify logging, encryption, retention, and data-handling controls meet the PSM intent.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: Deploy to staging and execute acceptance tests
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Deploy to staging and execute acceptance tests

step.sectionDescription: Deploy the exact candidate through the pipeline to a controlled non-production environment.
Execute smoke, integration, contract, and business acceptance tests for the deployable slice.
Record test data constraints, results, defects, and any accepted deviations.
Confirm logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, and alarms are emitted for critical paths.
Trigger representative failure and recovery scenarios to verify alert routing and diagnostic context.
Set practical thresholds and identify the team that responds to each alert.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: Create release, rollback, and communication plan
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Create release, rollback, and communication plan

step.sectionDescription: Define release scope, version, deployment sequence, approvals, maintenance window, and stakeholder communications.
Document rollback triggers, steps, data considerations, decision owner, and expected recovery time.
Rehearse rollback or recovery in non-production when the change affects data, interfaces, or critical availability.
Review release scope, risk, verification evidence, security findings, operational readiness, and rollback posture.
Capture go/no-go decision, approvers, constraints, and follow-up actions.
Confirm support and business stakeholders understand the release window and success criteria.
Publish runbooks for deployment, rollback, common incidents, access requests, and escalation.
Assign service ownership, on-call coverage, dashboards, alerts, service objectives, and support contacts.
Transfer repository, pipeline, and environment access according to the operating model.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: Execute production validation and close release
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Execute production validation and close release

step.sectionDescription: Deploy the approved release candidate using the documented pipeline and plan.
Perform post-deployment smoke checks, monitor health signals, and confirm business and technical success criteria.
Close the release or invoke rollback; record lessons and feed recurring issues to the PSM or generator backlog.

ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Review SLOs, telemetry, cost, and product outcomes

Capture actionable demand as visible service work items rather than inserting hidden work into a release plan.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: Triage and make service demand ready
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Triage and make service demand ready

step.sectionDescription: Record the demand source, impact, affected service, evidence, owner, and requested outcome on the Kanban board.

Where the item is maintenance, classify its purpose as corrective, preventive, adaptive, additive, or perfective; record any emergency temporary-restoration status; assign a class of service separately according to the board policy.
Refine the item until it meets the Ready policy and identify its likely disposition: operations-only response, the shortest safe model-driven change path, or a planned release backlog.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: Replenish, pull, and manage Kanban flow
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Replenish, pull, and manage Kanban flow

step.sectionDescription: At the replenishment cadence, select eligible items into Ready according to capacity, risk, class-of-service policy, and value; pull a ready item only when the downstream WIP control permits.

Use the board to manage work-item age, blocked work, service-level expectations, and reserved service capacity; an expedite item may displace other work only under the explicit expedite policy and must remain visible.

Hold a daily flow review and periodic service-delivery review using WIP, throughput, cycle time, work-item age, SLE attainment, arrival rate, blocked time, and expedite frequency; adapt the Definition of Workflow through an explicit improvement decision.
Triage impact, stabilize service, communicate status, and execute approved recovery actions.
Record incident timeline, affected scope, decisions, temporary modifications, and evidence.
Create permanent corrective, security, or change work for systemic causes and keep it visible after restoration.
Analyze contributing causes across requirements, models, transformation, generation, deployment, and operation.
Update controls, tests, model patterns, risk treatment, process guidance, or method profile as appropriate.
Place permanent corrective work on the Kanban board or deliberately commit it to a planned release, and verify reconciliation after any emergency downstream fix.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: Assess and route a maintenance change
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:purpose: Assess and route a maintenance change

step.sectionDescription: Classify the authoritative source as product/domain, architecture, platform, generator, artifact, or operations and confirm whether the item remains a bounded Kanban service item or is committed to a planned release.
Use traces and dependency ownership to identify impacted downstream levels and teams.

Send product-changing work to the Development and Delivery Process at the smallest affected phase or activity; after release, reconcile emergency downstream fixes into the authoritative source and close the service item only when evidence returns.

MF-01 — Opportunity and feasibility
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: A project can commit to a solution before value, feasibility, constraints, and alternatives are understood. Result: The endeavor is pursued, explored, redirected, or stopped with explicit evidence.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: A problem, opportunity, or change proposal exists.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: The endeavor is pursued, explored, redirected, or stopped with explicit evidence.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-02 — Serverless suitability, cost, risk, and provider decision
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Serverless and provider commitments can be made without workload, cost, risk, or exit analysis. Result: A serverless/hybrid/non-serverless and provider decision or bounded experiment is authorized.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: Business outcomes, constraints, and candidate workload are known enough to compare alternatives.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: A serverless/hybrid/non-serverless and provider decision or bounded experiment is authorized.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-03 — Situational method tailoring
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: One fixed process either overburdens a project or omits necessary controls. Result: A versioned method profile selects content, evidence depth, roles, and review triggers.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: Product, risk, team, platform, compliance, and delivery factors are assessable.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: A versioned method profile selects content, evidence depth, roles, and review triggers.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-04 — Product, release, and increment framing
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Modeling can become an end in itself without a bounded outcome and acceptance evidence. Result: A valuable vertical slice is ready with owners, risks, dependencies, and evidence.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: An authorized product and method profile exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: A valuable vertical slice is ready with owners, risks, dependencies, and evidence.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:patternSource: IBM RUP distinction between lifecycle phases and contained iterations
PMI Disciplined Agile continuous-delivery product lifecycle

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-05 — Event-driven domain discovery and CIM modeling
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Business meaning can be lost if software/provider structure is chosen before domain and requirement understanding. Result: An accepted computation-independent model expresses intent, behavior, policy, and governance.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: An increment is ready and domain participants/sources are available.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: An accepted computation-independent model expresses intent, behavior, policy, and governance.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-06 — CIM assurance and readiness
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: An incomplete or inconsistent CIM can propagate false certainty downstream. Result: The revision is accepted, reworked, or deferred with trace and findings.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: A candidate CIM revision and acceptance context exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: The revision is accepted, reworked, or deferred with trace and findings.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-07 — CIM to PIM transformation and reconciliation
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Automated refinement can overwrite human decisions or hide unresolved mappings. Result: A traceable PIM draft is merged or conflicts/manual decisions are explicit.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: An accepted CIM and transformation profile exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: A traceable PIM draft is merged or conflicts/manual decisions are explicit.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:selectionRule: required when using the MODRISS transform

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-08 — Platform-independent serverless architecture
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Serverless architecture needs explicit provider-independent services, contracts, state, integration, workflow, security, and operability. Result: An accepted provider-independent architecture is ready for capability mapping.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: A PIM draft and authoritative CIM/requirements trace exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: An accepted provider-independent architecture is ready for capability mapping.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-09 — PIM to PSM transformation and reconciliation
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Provider mapping can silently introduce unsafe defaults or lose refinements. Result: A traceable PSM draft is merged and mapping gaps/conflicts are explicit.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: An accepted PIM and chosen supported provider profile exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: A traceable PSM draft is merged and mapping gaps/conflicts are explicit.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-10 — AWS PSM refinement and assurance
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Generated provider resources require explicit security, networking, quota, observability, recovery, cost, and deployment decisions. Result: An accepted AWS PSM is ready for reproducible generation.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: A reconciled AWS PSM draft and PIM trace exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: An accepted AWS PSM is ready for reproducible generation.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-11 — Reproducible model-to-text generation
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Generated output cannot be trusted or reproduced without exact source, template, configuration, and manifest provenance. Result: A generated-draft baseline and traceable manifest exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: An accepted PSM revision and generator profile exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: A generated-draft baseline and traceable manifest exist.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-12 — Artifact completion and test in the small
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Generated scaffolds can be mistaken for complete, correct software. Result: Business logic and extensions are complete and component evidence is available.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: A generated baseline, trace, and manual-action report exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: Business logic and extensions are complete and component evidence is available.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-13 — Test in the large and release qualification
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Locally correct functions and templates may fail as an integrated serverless service. Result: System, acceptance, NFR, security, resilience, recovery, and operational evidence support a release decision.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: A candidate baseline can be deployed to a representative non-production environment.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: System, acceptance, NFR, security, resilience, recovery, and operational evidence support a release decision.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-14 — Progressive CI/CD and transition
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: A technically valid candidate can still fail during promotion or handover. Result: The release is progressively promoted, observed, recorded, and accepted for operation.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: An immutable qualified candidate and recovery plan exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: The release is progressively promoted, observed, recorded, and accepted for operation.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:patternSource: PMI Disciplined Agile continuous-delivery lifecycle: transition as a regular activity

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-15 — Operate, observe, control cost, and learn
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: A deployed serverless service needs operational ownership and feedback to remain valuable, reliable, secure, and economical. Result: Service/product outcomes, SLOs, risk, security, and cost are controlled and feed prioritized change.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: A release has operational ownership and telemetry.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: Service/product outcomes, SLOs, risk, security, and cost are controlled and feed prioritized change.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-16 — Incident, problem, and controlled change propagation
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Emergency or evolutionary changes can diverge models, generators, code, and the running service. Result: Service is restored where necessary and change is routed to the earliest authoritative source and re-evidenced.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: An incident, finding, dependency, or requested change exists.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: Service is restored where necessary and change is routed to the earliest authoritative source and re-evidenced.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-17 — Retirement, migration, and closure
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: A service can be switched off while data, consumers, access, resources, costs, or legal obligations remain. Result: Users, data, integrations, access, resources, cost, and evidence are migrated or closed and accepted.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: A retirement/replacement trigger and accountable product/service owners exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: Users, data, integrations, access, resources, cost, and evidence are migrated or closed and accepted.

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-18 — Kanban service-delivery and maintenance system
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Production, maintenance, and improvement demand competes with planned delivery, while invisible queues or emergency speed can bypass model, trace, and release controls and create permanent divergence. Result: Service demand is visualized on a Kanban board, made ready and pulled within WIP controls, resolved or routed, measured, and reconciled with authoritative sources and release evidence.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: A production service, an accepted operating baseline, service ownership, observability, and an explicit flow policy exist.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: Service demand is visualized on a Kanban board, made ready and pulled within WIP controls, resolved or routed, measured, and reconciled with authoritative sources and release evidence.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:selectionRule: required whenever MODRISS operates a production service; policy depth and support coverage are tailored
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:patternSource: Kanban Guide 2025 Definition of Workflow, WIP control, SLE, and flow metrics
PMI Disciplined Agile Lean lifecycle, flow guidance, and value-stream optimization
Ahmad et al. 2018 systematic mapping of Kanban in software engineering
SWEBOK v4.0a maintenance categories and emergency maintenance

ownedMethodContentMember.name: MF-19 — DevOps cross-process coordination
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Development and operations can optimize locally while release readiness, production feedback, change ownership, and retirement obligations fall between processes. Result: G7 handover, CI/CD evidence, telemetry, incident and maintenance change routing, learning, and G8 closure synchronize the two processes without merging their control systems.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: Development and Delivery and Operations and Maintenance have named owners and a shared product boundary.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: G7 handover, CI/CD evidence, telemetry, incident and maintenance change routing, learning, and G8 closure synchronize the two processes without merging their control systems.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:selectionRule: required whenever a live release is operated
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:patternSource: Faustino et al. 2022 DevOps and IT service-management evidence

ownedMethodContentMember.name: UF-01 — Integrated management, assurance, and evidence
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:description: Lifecycle tasks become disconnected without continuous planning, risk, quality, security, change, trace, and evidence management. Result: Decisions, dependencies, risks, findings, revisions, evidence, and improvement remain controlled throughout the run.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:initialContext: An authorized product/process run exists.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:resultContext: Decisions, dependencies, risks, findings, revisions, evidence, and improvement remain controlled throughout the run.
ownedMethodContentMember.modriss:selectionRule: continuous and required; depth is tailored

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Repeat delivery Activities—not Phases—for each selected release inside the single Active Product Construction and Evolution Phase. Operations and Maintenance independently sustains accepted live baselines.

nestedBreakdownElement.name: Continuous Kanban Service-Delivery and Maintenance System
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Production, maintenance, and improvement demand is visualized on the service Kanban board, made ready through explicit policies, and pulled only within WIP controls. Operations-only work may complete in this system; bounded product changes use the shortest safe MDE path and applicable release controls; broader changes are deliberately committed to a planned release.
Begin planned delivery only after the method profile, ownership, controls, and first increment hypothesis are accepted.
Begin the sequential Retirement phase only after retirement is authorized and in-flight development/release work is resolved or explicitly transferred.

After increment acceptance, either start the next capability slice or leave the engine for release assembly. Any downstream finding re-enters the smallest affected child process through the recorded change workflow.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: PIM refinement reveals missing CIM concepts for the increment.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Extend CIM via change workflow; re-run CIM EVL before re-transform.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: AWS constraints require PIM architecture changes.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Adjust PIM policies or integration; re-run PIM→PSM ETL.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Generated artifacts fail validation or deployment dry-run.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Fix PSM at source stage; regenerate artifacts.

At G7, the promoted release becomes an accepted live baseline owned by the Operations and Maintenance Process. This starts that ongoing process for the first release and updates its live-release set for later releases.

Route product-changing maintenance to the earliest authoritative Development and Delivery activity. Operations continues for the accepted baseline while the change is engineered, qualified, released, and returned with evidence.
Retain the last accepted operating baseline and return corrective work to the earliest affected delivery activity before requalification.
Start the next planned release from roadmap demand or service work deliberately committed to planned delivery; Operations and Maintenance continues for all accepted live baselines.

nestedBreakdownElement.name: PSM accepted for generation

nestedBreakdownElement.name: Increment accepted, reworked, or deferred
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:acceptanceCondition: Value, verification, security, operability, trace, and explicit exceptions are accepted for the exact increment.

nestedBreakdownElement.name: Release authorized, rejected, or exception accepted
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:acceptanceCondition: The exact immutable candidate and recovery, assurance, operational, and economic evidence are accepted.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:acceptanceCondition: The running release, support obligations, observability, recovery, and ownership are accepted.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: After the phase-embedded review/adapt stage, revolve the CIM engine for the next capability slice.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Update glossary, then replay information taxonomy and domain structure.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Behavior modeling reveals missing information items or entities.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Extend taxonomy and structure, then resume behavior surface.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Aggregate grouping exposes command/event ownership conflicts.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Adjust commands and events, then re-synthesize aggregates.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Process steps reference behavior not on the CQRS surface.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Add behavior elements, then rebuild process flows.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Context membership is incoherent across aggregates.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Revisit aggregates, then re-run context synthesis.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Requirements cannot be traced to domain or behavior elements.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Extend domain model, then re-link requirements.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: EVL or readiness findings identify blocking gaps.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Resolve at source stage; replay forward to readiness gate.

nestedBreakdownElement.name: PIM Modeling Engine
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:activityRefs: id_pim.ph1 id_pim.ph2 id_pim.ph3 id_pim.ph4 id_pim.ph5 id_pim.ph6

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: After the phase-embedded review/adapt stage, revolve the PIM engine for the next service slice.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Function contracts reference undefined schemas or event types.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Complete contracts, then update function bindings.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Functions need stores or access patterns not yet modeled.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Extend data architecture, then replay compute tasks.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: API routes need schemas or error mappings not defined.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Complete contracts, then remap API routes.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Channels reference producers/consumers not defined as functions.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Add compute targets, then rewire integration topology.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Public endpoints lack principals or auth policies.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Identify unprotected resources; add security bindings.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Policies require integration or compute changes.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Apply policy targets on integration/compute elements.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: PIM EVL or platform mapping reveals blocking gaps.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Jump to earliest affected assurance stage; replay to readiness.

nestedBreakdownElement.name: AWS PSM Modeling Engine
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:activityRefs: id_psm.ph1 id_psm.ph2 id_psm.ph3 id_psm.ph4 id_psm.ph5 id_psm.ph6

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: After the phase-embedded review/adapt stage, revolve the PSM engine for the next deployable slice.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Networking requires new IAM roles, KMS keys, or secrets.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Extend security baseline, then replay networking.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Lambda mappings reference unprovisioned tables or buckets.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Provision storage, then rewire compute event sources.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Functions need EventBridge rules not yet modeled.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Extend event fabric, then update Lambda targets.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: API integrations reference incomplete Lambda or authorizers.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Complete compute/identity, then rebuild API integrations.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Step Functions targets changed after compute phase.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Reconcile compute targets, then regenerate ASL and observability.

nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:condition: Integration views or PSM EVL reveal broken wiring.
nestedBreakdownElement.modriss:guidance: Repair at source resource stage; regenerate views before M2T.
When verification, approval, or operational rehearsal exposes a defect, correct the source PSM or artifact baseline, regenerate where necessary, and repeat the affected readiness stages.
